correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge4\) the all-positive pattern forces a linear forest. Given a prescribed positive subset T, contraction yields a quotient linear forest Q of negative edges. For \(k\ge4\) components, a complement spanning path exists by even-then-odd ordering of blocks along a path completing Q. At \(k=2\) or \(k=3\), an available nontrivial T-component can be reversed to avoid the sole unavoidable forbidden block adjacency; for \(k=1\) no connector is needed. This constructs every trace for all n and every T. VCdim=\(n-1\) follows from size bound and support witnessing; the online upper bound is \(n-1\) mistakes via remembering queried labels and predicting negative on new edges. Counts and exceptional \(n\le3\) cases are checked by explicit enumeration. The verifier exhaustively checks all supports for \(n\le6\) and all linear-forest supports for \(n\le7\), without substituting finite observation for proof.

value.rationale: The result solves every edge-query support of the natural Hamiltonian-path incidence class and supplies an all-parameter positive/negative completion property, exact static and adaptive shattering dimensions, and rigid maximum support count. These are not a parameter substitution from all-tree or all-cycle bounds: those larger classes may use non-spanning or branching witnesses. The known linear-forest generating function is explicitly separated from the central new completion theorem.
